summary: FerBo is a superconducting qubit combining a high-transparency Andreev weak link with an LC circuit, achieving simultaneous suppression of both relaxation and dephasing through hybridization of fermionic Andreev bound states with the bosonic electromagnetic mode. The qubit states have disjoint support in Andreev sector space and delocalized wavefunctions in phase, providing protection over a well-defined and experimentally accessible parameter regime.
motivation: Conventional superconducting qubits like the transmon and fluxonium suppress either charge noise or flux noise dephasing, but wavefunction delocalization increases coupling to dissipative channels, limiting coherence. Hardware-level protection schemes combining multiple degrees of freedom have stringent parameter requirements; this work explores whether Andreev bound state structure can relax those constraints.
method: An effective Hamiltonian couples the bosonic LC mode to a Josephson quasi-resonant level junction in the even-parity Andreev manifold. Numerical diagonalization and analytical perturbative analysis characterize the qubit's charge relaxation susceptibility $|\langle 0|n^|1\rangle|^2$ and flux dephasing susceptibility $\partial^2 E_{01}/\partial\phi_{\mathrm{ext}}^2$ across parameter space, with support from microscopic Bogoliubov-de Gennes calculations of SNS nanowire junctions.
result: Protection emerges when the circuit impedance satisfies $Z/R_Q \gtrsim 2E_C/(\pi\epsilon_r)$ and the junction transmission is high ($\tau \to 1$), suppressing charge relaxation susceptibility by four orders of magnitude at $\phi_{\mathrm{ext}}=0$ while achieving exponential dephasing suppression; the boundary coincides with an avoided crossing between first and second excited states where the ground and first excited states undergo a parity transition, causing the ground state to localize in the $|-\rangle$ Andreev sector while $|1\rangle$ occupies the $|+\rangle$ sector.
